LAW AND MOTION 301, NO APPEARANCES ON THIS MATTER. THE COURT ADOPTED ITS TENTATIVE RULING AS FOLLOWS: DEFENDANT VINCENT COLLINS' PETITION TO COMPEL ARBITRATION IS DENIED. IN THIS ACTION PLAINTIFF HAS BROUGHT ESSENTIALLY IDENTICAL FACT AND LEGAL CLAIM RELATED TO THIS SAME TRANSACTION AGAINST A THIRD PARTY NOT SUBJECT TO THE ARBITRATION AGREEMENT. PLAINTIFF ALLEGES THAT DEFENDANT AND THIRD PARTY KNEW SAME FACTS, THAT THOSE FACTS WERE MATERIAL, THAT NEITHER PARTY DISCLOSED THEM, AND THAT EACH PARTY HAD A DUTY TO DO SO, THEREFORE, THERE'S A DISTINCT POSSIBILITY OF CONFLICTING RULINGS IF THE CASES AGAINST THE DEFENDANT AND THE THIRD PARTY WERE TO PROCEED IN DIFFERENT FORA. BECAUSE THE ISSUES ARE IDENTICAL, IT MAKES NO SENSE TO STAY ONE OR THE OTHER FORUM, RATHER PLAINTIFF'S CASE AGAINST ALL DEFENDANTS SHOULD GO FORWARD IN COURT, THE ONE FORUM WITH THE ABILITY TO ADJUDICATE THE ENTIRE DISPUTE. PREVAILING PARTY IS TO PREPARE A FORM OF ORDER. JUDGE: PETER J. BUSCH, REPORTER: CAROL A. KAREN, CSR # 8189 (301/PJB)
